construct: In obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, asymmetric septal hypertrophy and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve create a dynamic LV outflow tract gradient. Reduced preload or afterload and increased contractility shrink the LV cavity and worsen obstruction, so the murmur intensifies with standing or Valsalva and decreases with squatting or increased afterload.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Young patient with exertional presyncope, first-degree family history of sudden cardiac death, asymmetric basal septal hypertrophy, and a murmur that intensifies when preload falls is classic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Mitral valve prolapse can become more prominent with reduced LV volume, but the echocardiographic asymmetric septal hypertrophy and harsh LVOT-type systolic murmur uniquely point to obstructive HCM.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Family history plus asymmetric septal hypertrophy and preload-sensitive LVOT murmur make obstructive HCM the single best diagnosis.
